# ADR-0129: Conditions and randomness are evaluated by the system, not interpreted by the LLM

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-05-29

**Context.** Response gating and chance-based mechanics involve probabilities and conditions. These could be described to the LLM (e.g. 'respond 10% of the time') and left to its judgment, or evaluated deterministically by the system.

**Decision.** Response conditions are evaluated by the system before LLM invocation; randomness is supplied by system tools (e.g. roll_effects), never generated by the LLM. The LLM either gets asked to respond or does not — it never sees the probability.

**Alternatives rejected.**
- *Let the LLM interpret probabilities/conditions ('roll for 30% chance')* — the LLM will always succeed, always fail, or pick by narrative preference — not true randomness; interpretation gives varying behavior by mood/context/model instead of consistency and predictability

**Consequences.** Response gating and chance outcomes are deterministic and reproducible; randomness has two timing contexts (response control before the LLM, in-response rolls via tools during generation). The LLM applies results rather than producing them. Mined from: /home/me/git/exoplace/hologram/docs/philosophy.md (202), /home/me/git/exoplace/hologram/docs/philosophy.md (174-175).
